newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes up but trading thin - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes up but trading thin - brokers.

text.p: Czech shares edged higher on Monday led by major issues but dealers said activity was low as the market was still overshadowed by uncertainty about the future of the embattled coalition government.
The PX50 rose 0.6 percent to 491.3 while the Reuters RPIX index of continuously traded shares rose 0.9 percent to 1,019.4.
"It's very very flat, nobody wants to trade...I think sentiment is for growth but people don't know what will happen in the market," said Ivo Suchy of ING Barings.
Monday's gainers were led by Komercni Banka which rose 57 crowns to 1,929, SPT Telecom, up 26 crowns to 3,025, and tobacco company Tabak which gained 78 crowns to 7,600.
On Monday, a new finance minister, Ivan Pilip, was named. Pilip has pledged to make reform of the capital markets as priority.
However, internal wrangling inside the centre-right coalition and a forthcoming vote of confidence in the government, has destabilised currency and equity markets.
